extracted.intended_audience: British public and policymakers (radio listeners and wartime citizens)
extracted.subtask_description: A news report of a wartime radio address outlining post-war policy proposals and priorities (demobilization, social insurance, reconstruction, foreign policy) delivered to the British public and government. Emphasizes sequencing of military objectives and planning for transition to peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sober public communication / avoid false promises
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolved not to give or to make all kinds of promises and to tell all kinds of fairy tales to you who have trusted me.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speak with reserve, avoid ungrounded promises; tell people truthfully rather than offering comforting but unrealistic pledges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceaseless preparedness and forethought
rubrics_metrics.description: It is our duty to peer through the mists of the future to the end of the war: and to try our utmost to be prepared by ceaseless effort and forethought for the kind of situations which are likely to occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continual planning for likely post-war scenarios; make arrangements now to meet future contingencies rather than reacting ad hoc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequencing of military priorities: defeat Hitler first, then Japan
rubrics_metrics.description: I can imagine that some time next year... we might beat Hitler. By which I mean, beat him and his powers of evil into death, dust and ashes. Then we shall immediately proceed ... to punish the greedy, cruel empire of Japan ... That will be our first and supreme task and nothing must lure us from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize the European Axis (Germany/Italy) before large-scale redeployment to the Far East; avoid diverting primary resources prematurely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-war tri-power leadership and world organization
rubrics_metrics.description: It would be our hope that the United Nations, headed by three great victorious powers, the British Commonwealth of Nations, the United States and Soviet Russia, should immediately begin to confer upon the future world organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiate immediate conferences among the major victors to design institutions that will safeguard against future wars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disarmament and legal accountability of guilty states
rubrics_metrics.description: Which is to be our safeguard against further wars by effectively disarming and keeping disarmed the guilty states, by bringing to justice the ... criminals and their accomplices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design mechanisms to disarm aggressive states and to prosecute major war criminals as part of post-war security arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restitution of pillaged resources and cultural treasures
rubrics_metrics.description: By securing the return to the devastated and subjugated countries of the mechanical resources and artistic treasures of which they have been pillaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reparative measures to restore economic means and cultural property to occupied/looted nations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avert widespread famine in ruined regions
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall also have a heavy task in trying to avert wide-spread famine in some, at least, of the ruined regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare food relief and agricultural recovery programs for devastated areas as a central element of post-war planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival of Europe via a Council with legal and military instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: We must try ... to make the Council of Europe, or whatever it may be called, into a really effective league, with all strongest forces concerned woven into its texture, with a high court to adjust disputes and with forces, armed forces, national or international or both, held ready to prevent renewed aggression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a Europe-wide body combining judicial dispute resolution and collective security forces to prevent future continental aggression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of small states through groupings/confederations
rubrics_metrics.description: Side by side with the great powers, there should be a number of groupings of states, or confederations which would express themselves ... making a council of great States and lesser States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design institutional arrangements so weaker nations' rights and interests are safeguarded—consider federations or confederations rather than leaving them isolated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid premature fixation on frontiers or exact post-war arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing could be more foolish than to plunge in ... prescribe the exact groupings of states or lay down precise machinery for their co-operation or, still more to argue about frontiers now while the war ... has not yet reached its full height.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay detailed territorial or structural decisions until more facts are known; concentrate on principles and tentative discussions now.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four years' plan for the transition period
rubrics_metrics.description: I am very much attracted to the idea that we should make and proclaim what might be four years' plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a fixed multi-year framework (suggested four years) to manage demobilization, reconstruction, and economic transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned partial demobilization with care to avoid past mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: There will certainly be a partial demobilization following on the defeat of Hitler, and this will raise the most difficult and intricate problems, and we are taking care in our arrangements to avoid the mistakes which were so freely committed last time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare detailed demobilization plans (timing, reintegration, employment) to avert the post-WWI slump and social dislocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of employment and fair reintegration for returning servicemen
rubrics_metrics.description: There will certainly be large numbers of men ... who will have to be brought back to their families and to their jobs or to other equally good jobs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure programs, job creation, and placement to return servicemen to civilian life with adequate employment and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: National compulsory insurance (unified social insurance)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must rank me and my colleagues as strong partisans of national compulsory insurance for all classes, for all purposes from the cradle to the grave. Every preparation, including, if necessary, a preliminary legislative preparation, will be made with the utmost energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move toward a unified, compulsory national insurance system covering welfare from birth to old age, with legislative groundwork prepared in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for full employment / 'no unemployment'
rubrics_metrics.description: Here let me remark that the employment is to have no unemployment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orient economic and reconstruction policies toward preventing unemployment; use public works, planning, and industrial policy to maintain jobs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deal with 'unemployables' and discourage idleness across classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Unemployables, rich or poor, will have to be toned up. We cannot afford to have idle people. Idlers at the top make idlers at the bottom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote social expectations and policies that discourage long-term idleness and encourage productive contribution from all classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural self-sufficiency and rural revival
rubrics_metrics.description: It is absolutely certain that we shall have to grow a larger proportion of our food at home. ... I hope to see a vigorous revival of healthy village life on the basis of these higher wages and of improved housing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in agriculture (wages, housing, techniques) to increase domestic food production and make rural life attractive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public health, family policy, and pro-natalist concern
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the most somber anxieties ... is a dwindling birth-rate. ... people must be encouraged ... care of the young and establishment of sound hygienic conditions of motherhood have a bearing upon the whole future of the race.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement public-health measures, maternal and child care, and policies encouraging larger families to secure demographic strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadened, liberal education with religious freedom retained
rubrics_metrics.description: I hope our education will become broader and more liberal. ... There is another element which should never be banished from our system of education ... Freedom of Religion. ... religion has been the rock in the life and character of the British people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand access and curriculum breadth; maintain freedom of thought and conscience in schools while preserving religion's role where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunities and widened access to advanced education
rubrics_metrics.description: It is in our power, however, to secure equal opportunities for all. Facilities for advanced education must be evened out and multiplied. Nobody who can take advantage of higher education should be denied this chance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove geographic and class barriers to higher education; test by fair competition yet provide equalized facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-release and life-long learning for workers and youth
rubrics_metrics.description: We must make plans for time release from industry so that our young people may have the chance to carry on their general education and also to obtain specialized education which will fit them better for their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable workers and youth to alternate work and study (time-release), supporting continuous training and specialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large-scale rebuilding of towns and cities as employment policy
rubrics_metrics.description: We have one large immediate task in the planning and re-building of our cities and towns. This will make a very great call on our resources in material and labor, but it is also an immense opportunity not only for improvement of our housing, but for employment of our people in the years immediately after the war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reconstruction as a deliberate employment and housing-improvement program; integrate into the four years' plan and protect insurance funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent post-war slump via forward projects and mixed public/private enterprise
rubrics_metrics.description: We must not be caught again that way. It is therefore necessary to have projects for the future employment of people ... that private enterprise and state enterprise are both able to play their parts to the utmost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare future-facing public projects, coordinate state and private enterprise roles, and maintain a pipeline of projects to sustain employment and demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: State role in ownership and balancing economic development
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a broadening field for state ownership and enterprise, especially in relation to monopolies of all kinds. The modern state will increasingly concern itself with the economic well-being of the nation ... a number of measures ... will enable the government to exercise a balancing influence upon development which can be turned on or off as circumstances require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use selective state ownership/regulation for monopolies and deploy fiscal/administrative levers to moderate economic cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit wartime technological and production advances in peacetime industry
rubrics_metrics.description: We have learned much about production under the stress of war. Mass production has been forced upon us ... Electrification of industry has been increased 50 per cent. ... improvements in wireless and the wonders of radio-location applied to the arts of peace ... There is civil aviation. There is forestry. There is transportation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate wartime innovations (mass production, electrification, radio/radar tech, etc.) into civilian industries and modernization efforts (transport, aviation, forestry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate post-war trade and currency policy with allies and Dominions
rubrics_metrics.description: Our fortunes will be greatly influenced by policies of the United States and of the British dominions, and we are doing our utmost to keep in ever closer contact with them. We have lately put before them ... some tentative suggestions for future management of exchanges and of new currency, which will shortly be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage allied partners early on trade and currency management to secure fair access to world markets and stable exchange arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect and redeem national wartime savings and honor financial obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: These savings of the nation arising from the thrift, skill or devotion of individuals are sacred. The state is built around them and it is duty of the state to redeem its faith in an equal degree of value. Those whose houses have been destroyed ... are entitled to compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safeguard citizens' savings (war bonds, nest eggs), ensure compensation for war losses, and maintain trust in public finance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heavier taxation may be needed but must preserve incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: We must expect taxation... heavier than it was before the war, but we do not intend to shape our plans or levy taxation in a way which, by removing personal incentive, would destroy initiative of peace and enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept higher post-war tax burdens while designing tax policies that preserve personal and entrepreneurial incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain focus on war effort; avoid premature peace preoccupation
rubrics_metrics.description: I must warn every one who hears me of ... the danger of ... appearing to be diverting our attention to a peace which is still remote and to the fruits of a victory which have still to be won while our Russian allies are fighting for dear life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While planning for peace, do not let public or political attention undermine or distract from ongoing military efforts; support allies engaged in current fighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comradeship and loyalty among nations as basis for post-war success
rubrics_metrics.description: If we act with comradeship and loyalty to our country and to one another ... we may be astonished at the progress ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize cooperative international relations and mutual loyalty among allies to secure successful reconstruction and peace.
